hypothesis:
The MLP expansion ratio has never been varied. `4 * config.n_embd` appears exactly twice per file in all 432 nodes of this campaign -- the ratio is hardcoded and has been constant since trial one, while depth (8/10/11/12/13/14), aspect ratio (36/39/42/51/64) and head dim (64/128/256) were all explored. It is the largest untouched structural axis in the model.

It matters most now, for two reasons. The MLP holds roughly 25M of the ~46M non-value-embedding parameters and is the model's biggest FLOPs consumer, so its width trades capacity against step count almost directly under a fixed 300-second budget. And the trade is now measurable: t0433 just demonstrated that throughput converts to bpb exactly as the token law predicts, with a +1.14% step gain producing -0.000494 against a predicted -0.000662 and a mechanism residual of +0.000168, inside the floor. So a width change can be decomposed cleanly into the throughput it buys or costs and the capacity it loses or gains, which is precisely the decomposition this campaign is equipped to make and has never had an untouched axis to apply it to.

This arm widens the MLP to 5x, and it is queued regardless of what the 3x arm returns. That is deliberate. A single point either side of an incumbent tells you a direction; it does not tell you whether the incumbent is an interior optimum or a value nobody ever questioned. The warmdown axis looked like an unfinished ramp for the whole campaign and turned out to be an interior optimum only once it was bracketed from above -- and three coordinates had been burned by then. Here the coordinates are cheap and the bracket can be built deliberately.

5x adds about 6.3M parameters and costs steps. Under the token law that debit is knowable in advance from the step count, so the capacity credit is measurable as the residual.
change_summary: A new MLP_RATIO = 5 constant, with both `4 * config.n_embd` sites in the MLP class reading `MLP_RATIO * config.n_embd`. Per-layer hidden width goes 2048 -> 2560. Identical mechanism to the 3x arm in the opposite direction, same guards, dry-run verified against the t0433 champion source.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
I expect this to lose, and the value is in how much. Steps should fall, the token law debits -0.0586*ln(steps/champion_steps), and whatever capacity buys shows up as the residual against that. If the loss is smaller than the throughput debit, extra width is genuinely worth something and 4x may be under-provisioned in a longer budget even though it is not here. If the loss is larger than the debit, width is actively harmful at this scale and 4x is above the optimum -- which would make the 3x arm's result a lower bound rather than a peak.
Large step change is expected and is the mechanism, not contention, provided it is consistent with the parameters added.
risk:
Cost is the main risk: this is a slot spent on an arm I expect to lose, purely to bracket. That is justified only if the bracket actually changes what I would do next, and it does -- 4x being an interior optimum versus 4x being above the optimum lead to different follow-ups, and I cannot distinguish them from the 3x arm alone.
Second risk: a wider MLP may OOM or trip the throughput guard's floor. Peak VRAM at 4x is about 35.7GB against 140GB, so headroom is ample and OOM is unlikely; a genuine slowdown is expected and the guard's 8.0 steps/s floor is well below the ~9.4 healthy rate, so a modest step loss will not trigger it -- but a large one might, and a guard abort here would be a true positive about cost rather than a false alarm.
